key_insight: Inverse PINNs can recover Manning friction reliably in 2D shallow-water flows with enough joint depth-velocity data, but 1D cases show a persistent bias that points to identifiability limits.
engineering_relevance: This benchmark tells hydrodynamics practitioners when sparse, noisy field measurements are sufficient for parameter estimation and when additional sensors or model redesign are needed.
method: Train a PINN to jointly infer the flow field and a positive scalar Manning friction coefficient.
Use a two-phase training strategy: first fit observations, then enforce shallow-water physics residuals.
Benchmark recovery under controlled changes in sparsity, noise, and observed variable type in 1D and 2D test cases.
evidence_signal: In the 2D case, friction errors stayed below 5% with at least 10 depth and velocity observations and noise up to 10% of the field standard deviation, while 50 observations remained stable even at 20% noise.
watch_item: Recovery drops sharply when only one variable is observed, and the 1D case retains about 15% positive bias regardless of data density, so identifiability checks are essential before deployment.
paper_title: How Sparse and How Noisy? Systematic Benchmarking of Inverse Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Manning Friction Estimation in Shallow Water Equations
